# Part of each of the three currencies spent.
#
#     400.00 USD from the 1.30 basis, spent at 1.45
#                                     520.00 cost      580.00 fetched     60.00 realized
#  46,500.00 HKD from the 1/6 basis, spent with the peg at 7.75, so at 26/155
#                                   7,750.00 cost    7,800.00 fetched     50.00 realized
#     900.00 CAD of rent, which realizes nothing: Canadian dollars are what
#                                   this book is kept in
#
# 46,500 divides by both 6 and 155, so the cost and what it fetched are each
# exact to the cent rather than rounded — the gain is 50.00 and not 50.00-ish.
#
# What is left is 600.00 USD costing 780.00, and 99,510.00 HKD costing
# 16,585.00. The US dollar is priced at 1.30 on both dates the sheet is drawn
# at, so its unrealized figure is 0.00 at each — the control. Only the Hong
# Kong dollar moves, and it moves both ways:
#
#     as of 2026-11-30, peg 7.85, at 26/157 — worth less than it cost
#     as of 2026-12-31, peg 7.75, at 26/155 — worth more
#
# `{usd_basis}` and `{hkd_basis}` are the guids of the two foreign earnings'
# cost bases, read from `fx-balances` after the first import.
2026-07-01 * "Subcontractor paid in US dollars, at 1.45"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank -400.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-520.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{usd_basis}"
	Expenses:Subcontractors 580.00 CAD
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD

2026-08-01 * "Subcontractor paid in Hong Kong dollars, the peg at 7.75"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:HKD Bank -46500.00 HKD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "HKD"
		share_price: "1/6"
		value: "-7750.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{hkd_basis}"
	Expenses:Subcontractors 7800.00 CAD
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD

2026-09-01 * "Rent, in Canadian dollars"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Expenses:Rent 900.00 CAD
	Assets:CAD Bank -900.00 CAD
